question: A designated portion of a relay race is called as _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Leg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **leg** refers to a designated portion or segment of a relay race. It is a critical term used in athletics to divide the race into sections for each team member.
 
• In a relay race, the total distance is divided into equal segments called "legs," which are run by individual team members.
 
• The performance in each **leg** contributes to the overall team result in the relay race. A strong performance by all runners ensures a higher chance of winning.
 
• Relay races commonly include 4x100 meters or 4x400 meters, where each runner completes a specific **leg** before passing the baton to the next runner.
 
• This term is specific to athletics and is not interchangeable with other options provided, such as "heat," which refers to a qualifying race, or "spikes," which are shoes worn by athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relay Races:**

 
 
• Relay races are team events in track and field where four athletes complete equal segments of the race, passing a baton to the next runner after completing their respective leg.
 
• The two most common relay events are the **4x100 meters** and **4x400 meters**. In the 4x100 meters relay, each runner covers 100 meters, while in the 4x400 meters relay, each runner covers 400 meters.
 
• Relay races require precise coordination during baton exchanges to avoid disqualification.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Terms:**
 
 
• **Heat:** Refers to a preliminary race used to qualify athletes for the final race. It is not related to a portion of the relay race.
 
• **Spikes:** Specialized shoes with spikes on the sole to provide better grip and traction on the track, aiding in faster sprints.
 
• **Lifting:** This term is unrelated to athletics and is typically associated with weightlifting or the act of picking something up.
 
 
 
• **History of Relay Races:**
 
 
• The concept of relay races originates from ancient Greece, where messengers ran in relays to deliver messages over long distances.
 
• Modern relay races became part of the Olympic Games in the early 20th century, with the 4x100m and 4x400m events introduced in 1912.
 
 
 
• **Rules and Techniques:**
 
 
• Each runner must run entirely within their designated lane during their leg of the race, particularly in the 4x100 meters relay.
 
• The baton must be passed within a designated zone of 20 meters, and dropping the baton or passing it outside this zone leads to disqualification.
 
• In the 4x400 meters relay, runners may merge into the innermost lane after the first leg is completed.
